evidence.summary: ROLES maps viewer to {read}, editor to {read, write}, admin to {read, write, manage_roles}.
can(role, permission) returns whether the role's permission set contains the permission; an unknown role has no permissions.
set_role(actor_role, target, role) raises PermissionError('only admins manage roles') unless the actor has manage_roles, then writes target['role'] = role without checking that role is a known role.

architecture.backend: single Python module, pure functions over role names; no user store

features.name: Roles and permission checks
features.description: Three roles (viewer, editor, admin), each a set of permissions, and one check of whether a role may do something.
features.observed_behaviour: can(role, permission) looks the role up in ROLES and tests membership; unknown roles get nothing.
features.business_logic: viewer: read. editor: read, write. admin: read, write, manage_roles. Deny by default.
features.integration: Becomes the unified role set and the single permission check.

features.name: Change a user's role (admins only)
features.description: An admin assigns a role to another record.
features.observed_behaviour: set_role(actor_role, target, role) refuses with PermissionError unless the actor's role has manage_roles; otherwise sets target['role'].
features.business_logic: Only manage_roles (admin) may change roles. The new role is not validated (any string is accepted). The actor is identified only by a role string, not an authenticated user.
features.integration: Needs the authenticated caller (from a session), the unified user store, and validation of the new role.

error_handling.behaviour: can() returns False; set_role() stores it anyway

unknowns: Roster has no user store or sign-in; where target records live is not in the source.
Whether an admin may demote themselves (or the last admin) is not decided by the source; set_role allows it.
